descriptions.text: Over $16 million drained by a fake that tricked their vaults using their own permissions. AlexLab got rekt - again. Last year it was a leaked key, this time it’s bad logic. Two exploits, two attack vectors - same protocol, still not learning.

On June 6, 2025, ALEX Protocol was attacked due to a vulnerability in its on-chain self-listing verification logic, which is constrained by limitations on Stacks. As a result, multiple asset pools were drained, with total losses amounting to approximately $8.37 million.

ALEX Lab’s June 6, 2025 self-listing exploit on Stacks drained liquidity pools after the protocol treated a mined-transaction signal as proof that a token listing was valid. The official grant terms list 8,403,867.57 STX, 21.85 sBTC, 149,850.00 aUSD, and 2.80 aBTC as unrecovered assets. ALEX’s self-listing verification path treated was-tx-mined-compact as if it proved that a token deployment or execution was valid. The Stacks Foundation later clarified that the function only shows whether a transaction was mined, not whether the target code executed successfully, so attacker-controlled token logic was admitted into the vault path.

On June 6, 2025, AlexLab on the Stacks smart contract layer was exploited for at least $8.4M after a flaw in its self-listing feature let an attacker list a malicious token. The attacker bypassed validation, drained assets from vaults through swaps and farms, and moved funds out. Full user reimbursement was later announced, but no primary on-chain data is present. AlexLab's self-listing feature allowed new tokens to be listed without robust verification of contract behavior. ALEX Lab lost $8.3 million in various currencies after an attacker exploited a flaw in the project's smart contracts that allowed them to create a malicious token. They drained a number of pools on the protocol, amounting to around $8.3 million. ALEX announced they would reimburse stolen user funds. This is the second exploit affecting ALEX Labs, after a thief stole around $2 million in May 2024.
